headline: Use {arm:brisk-s.few} for the turn router: of the {n_candidates|words} configurations it is the only one inside every gate, at {cost_per_month.brisk-s.few|usd_whole} a month.
lede: It clears balanced accuracy by {criteria.overall.brisk-s.few.gap|abs|pts} points and its weakest cell, Complex × News, by {criteria.cell_floor.brisk-s.few.complex.news.gap|abs|pts} points, both beyond their intervals. The call moves only if its p95 latency, read without an interval, proves slower in production, or if the cell floor were lowered enough to admit the cheaper {arm:nano-xs.few}.

caveats.material_if: Only if the recommended configuration's true p95 latency sits more than {criteria.p95.brisk-s.few.gap} above today's {criteria.p95.brisk-s.few.value}: then nothing passes every gate and the latency budget itself needs a decision.

Only if a fresh run reads the recommended configuration's balanced accuracy more than {criteria.overall.brisk-s.few.gap|abs|pts} points lower than today. Its interval clears the gate today, but being the pick of {n_candidates|words} pulls its estimate up.

Only for the comparisons between configurations (the cell gaps to {arm:nano-xs.few}, the effects of model and prompt), which are read unpaired and so wider than paired; the call reads each configuration against declared lines and does not rest on them.

decision.text: Ship {arm:brisk-s.few} on all turns. Balanced accuracy is {measure.balanced_accuracy.brisk-s.few.mean} ({overall_interval.balanced_accuracy.brisk-s.few.interval|interval}, derived), every cell holds its floor and p95 latency is {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.few.p95}.

{arm:nano-xs.few} would cost {cost_per_month.nano-xs.few|usd_whole} a month but misses the floor in Complex × News at {criteria.cell_floor.nano-xs.few.complex.news.value}, clear of its interval. {arm:atlas-m.few}, {arm:atlas-m.rubric} and {arm:brisk-s.rubric} are more accurate but blow the {criteria.p95.threshold} latency budget. The rest miss the accuracy gate.

The weakest margin is {weakest.arm} on {weakest.criterion}: {weakest.value} against {weakest.threshold}, {weakest.margin|abs|pts} points. Its interval clears the line, but the pick of {n_candidates|words} reads high by chance. The latency headroom of {criteria.p95.brisk-s.few.gap} is relatively larger yet matters as much, because no interval says how firm it is.
Ship now; in parallel, measure the recommended configuration's p95 latency on production traffic with an interval, and re-run it on fresh cases to confirm the accuracy clearance.

claims.text: {arm:brisk-s.few} is the only configuration that passes every gate; each other configuration fails at least one.

evidence.caption: Each configuration against each gate, with the figure that binds where it fails or is borderline.

claims.text: The cheaper {arm:nano-xs.few} would save {price.nano-xs.few.brisk-s.few.balanced_accuracy.monthly_cost_gap|abs|usd_whole} a month if it passed, but it trails {arm:brisk-s.few} by {compare.brisk-s.few.nano-xs.few.accuracy.cells.complex.news.difference|abs|pts} points in Complex × News, where it misses the floor.

evidence.caption: Accuracy, Brisk-S few-shot minus Nano-XS few-shot, in each cell, with unpaired intervals; positive rows favour Brisk-S few-shot.

claims.text: The most accurate configurations are out on latency alone: {arm:atlas-m.rubric} reaches {measure.balanced_accuracy.atlas-m.rubric.mean} balanced accuracy at a p95 of {measure.latency_ms.atlas-m.rubric.p95}.

evidence.caption: Balanced accuracy against p95 latency (log axis) for every configuration, with both gate lines. Nano-XS few-shot also sits inside both; the cell floor, not drawn here, removes it.

claims.text: What a prompt buys depends on the model: few-shot examples lift Nano-XS by {lever.prompt.nano-xs.zero.nano-xs.few.balanced_accuracy.effect|pts} points, while rubric + reasoning takes {lever.prompt.nano-xs.few.nano-xs.rubric.balanced_accuracy.effect|abs|pts} points back from it yet adds accuracy for Atlas-M.

evidence.caption: Change in balanced accuracy from moving one setting, for Atlas-M and Nano-XS, and how each change differs across the other setting; unpaired intervals, descriptive.

claims.text: Every accuracy clearance of {arm:brisk-s.few} is settled at today's size; the latency budget is the one line no interval reads.

evidence.caption: Each line Brisk-S few-shot is read against: its distance, the cases that would settle it, and how often a fresh run of today's size would read the other side.

explore.binds: Whether the cheaper Nano-XS few-shot is admitted
explore.outcome: Read on point estimates: at or below {criteria.cell_floor.nano-xs.few.complex.news.value} Nano-XS few-shot becomes the call; up to {criteria.cell_floor.brisk-s.few.complex.news.value} Brisk-S few-shot holds; above that nothing passes.

explore.binds: Whether any configuration passes, and which
explore.outcome: Below {criteria.p95.brisk-s.few.value} nothing passes. Any looser budget admits slower, more accurate configurations, but Brisk-S few-shot stays the call: they cost more and nothing declared prices accuracy above the gate.

explore.control: The gate on balanced accuracy, declared at {criteria.overall.threshold}
explore.outcome: Above {criteria.overall.brisk-s.few.value} nothing passes; at any lower line Brisk-S few-shot stays the call.

omitted.why: No gate reads them and the decision has no rule weighing them; they stay in the appendix.
They describe which labels get swapped; no gate reads them and they do not change the call.

omitted.what: Cost ranking among the configurations that fail a gate
omitted.why: A failed configuration is out before price; only Nano-XS few-shot is priced, as a labelled what-if.

omitted.what: Brisk-S rubric + reasoning's small accuracy gain over few-shot
omitted.why: It is out on latency, so the gain is unavailable.

omitted.what: Model and prompt effects for Brisk-S
omitted.why: They follow the same pattern as Atlas-M's; the full lever table is in the appendix.

next.text: Measure {arm:brisk-s.few}'s p95 latency on production traffic, repeated enough to put an interval on it.
next.settles: Whether its {criteria.p95.brisk-s.few.gap} of headroom under the budget is real; if not, nothing passes every gate and the budget or the accuracy gate needs a decision.

next.text: Re-run {arm:brisk-s.few} on {settle.criteria.overall.brisk-s.few.overall.cases_needed_two_sided_80|int} fresh cases, the size that settles its balanced-accuracy clearance four times in five.
next.settles: Whether the clearance survives being the pick of {n_candidates|words} configurations.

next.text: Add Complex × News examples to {arm:nano-xs.few}'s prompt and re-run the full matrix at today's size.
next.settles: Whether it clears that cell's floor and firms up its borderline balanced accuracy; only then is the saving of {price.nano-xs.few.brisk-s.few.balanced_accuracy.monthly_cost_gap|abs|usd_whole} a month on the table.

method.text: Each configuration labelled {scoreboard.brisk-s.few.cases|int} turns once, none lost; the matrix crosses complexity (Simple, Medium, Complex) with domain (Science, Conversational, News), and each cell holds the same count for every configuration.
A turn is correct when the predicted complexity and domain label matches the gold label. Accuracy is read per cell; balanced accuracy is the plain mean of the cells.

Cell accuracy carries a stated half-width at {overall_interval.balanced_accuracy.brisk-s.few.level}. Balanced accuracy's interval is derived from its cells (the root of their squared standard errors over their count), so it is called derived. Comparisons between configurations are unpaired and uncorrected for multiplicity.

None was set after the results: balanced accuracy at least {criteria.overall.threshold}, accuracy at least {criteria.cell_floor.threshold} in every cell, p95 latency at most {criteria.p95.threshold}. A figure on the passing side whose interval crosses its line passes and is called borderline.
One p95 per configuration, stated with no interval and no count of the requests behind it.
Measured cost per million routed turns. Monthly figures read the declared volume of {meta.volume_per_month} a month; the input does not say what that volume counts, and it is read here as turns.
There is no production router or control, and no mix of configurations by cell was run.
